To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transverse polarization can be large for the penguin-dominated charm B decays into vector-vector, axial-vector-axial-vector or vector-axial-vector final states, and that there is a wide variety of charmless B decays into axial-vector mesons within the reach of the B factories.

the transverse polarization fractions for the B → V V decays can be sizable, the B → V A decays are dominated by the transverse polarization states, the branching ratios of the B → A A modes are generally small, but the B → A V decays are promising.

the QCD factorization approach can accommodate large transverse polarization fractions for penguin-dominated VV modes by including the penguin-annihilations contributions and that the QCD-factorization approach is a powerful tool for studying B→ AV decays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of charmless B decays into two vector and two axial-vector meson final states.
the study of the branching ratios and the polarization in the B → V V, VA, AA decays within QCD factorization.
the study of B decays into two vector or two axial-vector states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many modes which can be studied at B factories and which will be useful in testing QCD factorization and in extracting the weak phases.
the B → V V and B → A A decays are very interesting and can be studied in great detail by B factories.

QCD factorization provides an excellent framework for studying the branching ratios and polarizations of B → VV, VA and AA modes, with the only exception being the K 1 K* decays, which are dominated by the annihilation contributions and thus are not calculable in the framework of Q.C.D factorization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polarization of B → VV decays can be large, and the transverse polarization can be large for some penguin-dominated charm- less B decays.
QCD factorization with next-to-leading-order corrections can provide an adequate description of the data.

the polarization states of B → VV and VA decays are sensitive to the relative sizes of the tree, penguin and annihilation amplitudes, and the polarization states of the B → AA decay can provide information on the axial-vector decay constants of the 1P 1 axial-vector states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QCD factorization can provide a reasonable description of the data, if the nonfactorizable corrections are taken into account.
the transverse polarization fractions of penguin-dominated VV decays can be large.
there are many modes with large transverse polarization fractions, and many other modes with large longitudinal polarization fractions.
